title: Three.js Immersive 3D Experience Design
summary: Three.js specific design rules, performance guidelines, and implementation patterns for immersive 3D web experiences including r128 CDN requirements, GLTF loading, animation loops, and shader patterns.
instructions: Use Three.js r128 CDN for stability. Do not use newer versions without verifying CapsuleGeometry support (r142+).
Import pattern: use ES modules from CDN (importmap) or the npm package (@types/three for TS).
OrbitControls: always load via ES module import path 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js'. Never use window globals.
Loading strategy: load GLTF models via GLTFLoader, show loading progress with THREE.LoadingManager before revealing scene.
Animation loop: use requestAnimationFrame inside a single render loop; do not create multiple loops.
Performance: keep polygon count under 100k for web, use BufferGeometry, reuse materials and geometries with instancing.
Dispose pattern: always call geometry.dispose(), material.dispose(), texture.dispose() on unmount to prevent GPU memory leaks.
R3F (@react-three/fiber): use Canvas component, declarative JSX for Three.js elements, useFrame for animation loops.
R3F Drei: import helpers from @react-three/drei (OrbitControls, Gltf, Text, Float, MeshDistortMaterial) for common patterns.
Responsive 3D: handle window resize with window.addEventListener('resize', onResize) updating camera.aspect + renderer.setSize.
Mobile performance: reduce pixel ratio (renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2))), simplify geometry on mobile.
Lighting: use 1-3 lights max for performance. Prefer directional + ambient combination over point lights.
Shadows: enable shadow maps only when needed. Use PCFSoftShadowMap for quality, BasicShadowMap for performance.
Immersive landing pages: use Three.js as hero background with subtle auto-rotating scene, particle systems, or floating geometry.
Post-processing: use EffectComposer from three/addons/ for bloom, SSR, and color grading — keep passes under 4 for performance.
No full-page Three.js: always overlay UI/HTML on top of the canvas; don't render DOM elements inside the 3D scene.
GLTF pipeline: use gltf-transform or Draco compression for production models. Target under 2MB per model.
Interaction: use Raycaster for mouse/touch interaction with 3D objects. Keep raycaster far distance reasonable.
Loading states: show skeleton or blur-up placeholder while 3D scene loads; don't flash unloaded white canvas.
SEO fallback: provide screenshot/image fallback when JavaScript is disabled (noscript tag with poster image).
For product showcases: use orbit controls with auto-rotate, environment maps (HDR) for realistic reflections.
For data visualization: use 3D scatter plots, bar charts with extrusion, or globe visualizations with proper color scales.
Accessibility: provide aria-label on canvas describing the 3D scene, respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing auto-rotation.
evidenceRequirements: Three.js version being used (check package.json or CDN import)
